sources.author: Harrison Chase
sources.headline: Co-founder & CEO @ LangChain
sources.post_summary: Discussed the rapid evolution of AI agents, highlighting how multi-step reasoning and tool-use capabilities are becoming production-ready. Shared benchmarks showing 3x improvement in agent reliability over the past quarter and emphasized the shift from chatbots to autonomous systems.

sources.author: Simon Willison
sources.headline: Independent AI researcher & creator of Datasette
sources.post_summary: Posted about the growing complexity of AI infrastructure, warning that many teams are over-engineering agent systems when simpler retrieval + prompting approaches still deliver strong results. Shared lessons from recent production deployments.

sources.author: Santiago Valdarrama
sources.headline: AI Engineer & Educator
sources.post_summary: Shared a practical walkthrough of building reliable AI agents using open-source frameworks, focusing on error handling, state management, and evaluation loops. Included code snippets and real-world failure cases from recent projects.

sources.author: Clem Delangue
sources.headline: Co-founder & CEO @ Hugging Face
sources.post_summary: Highlighted new Hugging Face tools for deploying and monitoring AI agents at scale, including inference endpoints and evaluation dashboards. Stressed the importance of observability in production AI systems.

sources.author: Alex Hormozi
sources.headline: Founder @ Acquisition.com
sources.post_summary: Discussed how modern GTM teams are replacing traditional SDRs with automated outbound sequences and AI-driven qualification. Emphasized building systems that scale without linear headcount increases.

sources.author: Elena Verna
sources.headline: Growth Advisor | Ex-MongoDB, Amplitude, SurveyMonkey
sources.post_summary: Shared a framework for aligning product-led growth with outbound motions, highlighting how RevOps teams should own both PLG signals and sales sequences to reduce CAC.

sources.author: Udi Ledergor
sources.headline: Chief Evangelist @ Gong | Ex-Check Point
sources.post_summary: Broke down how revenue teams are using conversation intelligence data to build automated playbooks that trigger personalized outbound at scale, moving beyond static sequences.

sources.author: April Dunford
sources.headline: Positioning Expert | Author of Obviously Awesome
sources.post_summary: Explained why content strategy must be embedded into GTM engineering rather than treated as a separate marketing function, using examples of how positioning drives outbound messaging.

sources.author: Kyle Poyar
sources.headline: Operating Partner @ OpenView
sources.post_summary: Analyzed how top-performing SaaS companies are restructuring RevOps to include GTM engineering roles responsible for building and maintaining outbound infrastructure and automation.

sources.author: Sahil Lavingia
sources.headline: Founder @ Gumroad
sources.post_summary: Sahil shared his decision to step back from day-to-day operations at Gumroad to focus on writing and smaller experiments. He reflected on the tradeoffs of scaling a company versus staying small and shipping personally meaningful work.

sources.author: Danny Postma
sources.headline: Founder @ Headlime & Indie Maker
sources.post_summary: Danny documented launching a new AI product in under 10 days as a solo founder. He broke down the tech stack, customer acquisition channels, and early revenue numbers while sharing lessons on speed and validation.

sources.author: Vic Vijayakumar
sources.headline: Ex-Meta → Solo Founder
sources.post_summary: Vic wrote about leaving Meta to build independently. He detailed his first 90 days as a solo developer, including choosing a problem space, validating with users, and the mental shift from big-tech stability to founder uncertainty.

sources.author: Pieter Levels
sources.headline: Indie Maker @ Levels.io
sources.post_summary: Pieter posted weekly updates on multiple micro-SaaS products he's running solo. He shared real-time metrics, feature experiments, and how he prioritizes which products to double down on versus sunset.

sources.author: Sara Mauskopf
sources.headline: Founder & CEO @ Once Upon
sources.post_summary: Sara discussed her transition from big tech PM roles into founding a consumer app. She highlighted the skills that transferred and the new muscles she had to build around fundraising, hiring, and product direction as a first-time founder.
